To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have synthesized and tested two inhibitors designed to bind the general acid or base in the active site of a GH99 enzyme, and that the inhibitors do not bind as expected.
we have synthesized and evaluated two mechanism‐inspired inhibitors for GH99 enzymes and that the results of our work have highlighted the limitations of this approach.

1) the design of mechanism‐based inhibitors for family 99 endo‐mannanases and endo‐mannosidases is challenging because of the lack of structural information and 2) the design of inhibitors for these enzymes based on a two‐step catalytic mechanism has been unsuccessful.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of mechanism‐based enzyme inhibitors, and their application to the study of glycoside hydrolysis.
the design and synthesis of inhibitors for family 99 endo‐mannanases and endo‐mannosidases, which cleave α‐1,2 mannose linkages in the core of N‐glycans.

the design and synthesis of inhibitors for glycoside hyrdrolase enzymes that are involved in the processing of complex carbohydrates, and with understanding the structural basis of their interactions with these enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two‐step mechanism for GH99 enzymes, while plausible and consistent with the observed inhibition of these enzymes by iminosugars, has not been demonstrated and is not yet proven.

mechanism‐inspired design of inhibitors for GH99 enzymes has failed to produce a potent and selective inhibitor, although the design has been successful in providing a detailed understanding of the mechanism of action of the enzymes.
the design and synthesis of inhibitors based on the proposed mechanism of GH99 family members is challenging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for GH99 endoα‐1,3/1,2‐man‐nanses, iminosugar inhibitors are not effective and that the design of inhibitors for these enzymes is a challenge.
, for GH99 enzymes, the design of inhibitors based on mechanism‐inspired principles is not straightforward.
the two‐carboxylate catalytic mechanism is not amenable to the design of inhibitors that can be used to probe the role of individual catalytic residues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two‐step mechanism is likely to be more complicated than previously thought, and that the two catalytic carboxylic acids may not be the only acid/base catalysts involved in catalysis.
, for GH99 endo α‐1,2 mannosidases and ‐mananases, it is difficult to achieve a high degree of specificity in the design of inhibitors targeting the general acid/base catalytic mechanism.

the two‐step mechanism is not the only one that can be envisaged for this family of enzymes, and that the mechanism‐based inhibitor strategy may need to be modified to take into account other potential mechanisms of action.
